analysis.title: US October CPI: another hot report
key_insights: US headline CPI printed at 0.35% MoM SA in October, above CACIB's 0.29% forecast and the Bloomberg average consensus of 0.27%. YoY is not available because October 2025 data is missing due to last year's government shutdown.

Core CPI printed at 0.30% MoM SA, above CACIB's 0.26% forecast and the Bloomberg average consensus of 0.22%. Core 3M annualised rose to 3.75% from 3.41% in September, after dipping below 2% in July and August.
CACIB sees the report as genuinely firm. Volatile components (airfares, lodging, car rental, wireless) were softer than in recent months, so noise does not explain the upside.

Services rose 0.34% MoM SA vs CACIB's 0.25% forecast, driving the core surprise. Transportation services rose 0.84% vs 0.24% forecast, led by car insurance (0.71% vs -0.48% forecast) and intracity transportation (6.63% vs 1.17%). Recreation services rose 0.88% vs 0.37%.

Core goods rose 0.16% MoM SA vs CACIB's 0.25% forecast, mostly because used cars fell -1.22% vs a forecast +0.46%. CACIB sees limited broad-based pass-through from high energy prices to core goods so far.
Shelter rose 0.30% MoM SA, 6bp above CACIB's preview forecast. OER rose 0.32% (0.35% in September) and rent rose 0.20%. CACIB is unsure OER prints above 0.3% will persist but says it bears watching.
Food rose 0.47% MoM SA vs CACIB's 0.34% forecast and 0.05% in September. Food away from home rose 0.52% and food at home 0.44%, led by meats, poultry, fish and eggs.

Energy rose 0.70% MoM SA vs CACIB's 0.57% forecast. Motor fuel rose 0.73% vs 0.57% forecast. CACIB expects YoY energy CPI to peak in May at 23.5% and stay in double digits through February. The path depends heavily on the Iran war and oil and gas prices.

Outlook: CACIB sees headline staying below a May peak and hovering in the mid-3% YoY range through Q1 2027. Core is expected in a 2.7-2.9% YoY band through Q1 2027, with modest improvement later in 2027.
Fed: CACIB says the October upside surprise on top of a firm September should basically lock in a 25bp hike in December, its base case. It questions why the Fed did not hike in October.

Governor Waller's comments raise the possibility of a 50bp move, but CACIB is unsure the data meets the bar for a jumbo hike from the broader Committee. CACIB sees a possibility of consecutive hikes in December and January instead of its base case of December and March.

PCE: CACIB awaits Friday's PPI to finalise estimates, but the firm CPI points to a relatively firm PCE. Computer software and accessories CPI fell -1.5% MoM, a second decline in three months. This category weighs more in PCE and may signal AI-linked price pressures are past a peak.
